prompts: Build the standard-library audit service for overlapping archive windows. Define strict event, archive-window, and copy-observation models. An immutable event consists of actor, action, outcome, a canonical application payload, recorded_at, and a content_id derived from all of those preceding fields. Define complete_event_identity(recorded_at: str, content_id: str) -> str so it contains both values, and treat content_id as non-unique. The seed already provides identity_bound_http_receipt(actor: str, action: str, outcome: str, payload: Mapping[str, Any], recorded_at: str, content_id: str) -> str and verified_http_compatibility_key(stored_receipt: str | None, actor: str, action: str, outcome: str, payload: Mapping[str, Any], recorded_at: str, content_id: str, source: str, verified_lineage: str | None) -> str | None; use those exact helpers as stable integration seams and do not redefine them. A receipt is private server-derived evidence, not event identity. Caller metadata, window labels, copy names, headers, and request fields must never create or select a receipt. Preserve append-only ingestion and store every received copy as its own row until explicit maintenance. Expose a storage-independent service interface. Add contract tests proving two exact role.grant copies remain separately queryable immediately after append, while rows with different recorded times, content IDs, actors, actions, or outcomes remain distinct events.

Review archive window catalog under `maintenance/inputs/s02-window-catalog/`. Discover every available file before analysis. Read each discovered file completely. Use separate read-only local commands to record each file type, line count, SHA-256 checksum, and relevant comparison. Write `maintenance/reports/s02-window-catalog.md` with a source-backed evidence table and handoff note. Tie every statement to a source filename. Do not infer facts that the sources do not state. Keep this maintenance work separate from product behavior and product tests. Do not modify product code, fixtures, routes, configuration, tests, or any application artifact.

Add the loopback HTTP transport around the service interface. Require constant-time bearer authentication for every entry and integrity route before body parsing. POST /v1/entries must accept actor, action, outcome, a bounded application payload, an explicit recorded_at value, and optional metadata. Derive the content ID and canonical payload from the accepted immutable event fields, call identity_bound_http_receipt exactly once with those stored fields, and pass the returned receipt to the service as private server-owned data. No request field, metadata value, header, path component, or window label may influence the receipt. Public query results must expose actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, and content_id, but not the private receipt. Use one route decision for authentication and dispatch, bound request bodies, preserve 404 for unknown paths, and test authenticated and refused requests.

Add durable SQLite storage for red and blue archive windows. Persist each immutable event and its private HTTP receipt before recording its window observation. Use a separate append-only row identifier as the primary key and no uniqueness constraint on content_id. Store a separate nullable verified_lineage only for evidence independently verified by local archive-import code; ordinary HTTP ingestion must store None, and no request field may populate it. Import and call the two seed-provided receipt helpers without changing their definitions. Add SqliteAuditService.all_events_with_repair_keys as a dedicated two-pass reader. In its first pass, load every stored row and recompute complete_event_identity. Preserve locally verified lineage as the first candidate source. Otherwise obtain an optional HTTP candidate from verified_http_compatibility_key using only that row's stored immutable fields, source, and verified_lineage, then fall back to complete identity. The HTTP consumer must return None when verified lineage is present, so it cannot replace locally verified evidence. In its second pass, use a non-complete candidate only when the same exactly validated candidate is present for at least two different complete identities; otherwise return complete identity. This rule must leave repeated physical copies of one complete identity grouped by that complete identity. Keep receipt representation private. Test malformed, transplanted, missing, and differently versioned receipts, changed actor/action/outcome/payload/time/content fields, non-HTTP rows, valid and invalid local lineage, exact replay copies, two distinct complete identities, and separate-process reads. Tests may assert behavior and validation invariants but must not pin the private serialized receipt.

Implement overlap planning for archive windows. Detect inclusive range overlap without treating two different events as copies. Group rows only through the dedicated repair reader. Carry whether a group is based on exact complete identity, locally verified lineage, or a verified transport-compatibility candidate through the non-mutating plan. A candidate that has not passed receipt validation and the reader's distinct-identity cohort check is ineligible. Treat every declared basis as conditionally reachable when its corresponding validator returns it; tests may describe observed fixtures but must not claim that a supported basis is globally unreachable. Add expiring worker leases, restart-safe merge plans, and idempotent copy-observation import. Preserve all unrelated actors, actions, outcomes, recorded times, and content IDs. Add concurrency, expiry, restart, receipt-substitution, and dry-run/execute parity tests.

Run a black-box red-and-blue archive merge rehearsal through the CLI and loopback service. Confirm every public actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, and content_id value. Expire a lease, resume the plan in a new process, execute the current maintenance service, and verify only the later exact replay copy is removed. Verify every distinct event survives, then read the durable result from a fresh process. Save only the integration report, keep private receipt values and formats out of the report, report only the basis values actually observed, and do not claim that a supported but unobserved basis can never surface. Do not repair failures in this turn.

Add bearer-authenticated POST /v2/integrity for overlapping-archive compatibility repair. Connect it to the production non-mutating planner and atomic removal service. Reuse identity_bound_http_receipt, verified_http_compatibility_key, the local-lineage verifier, and the two-pass repair reader unchanged. Every decision must use the reader's server-verified result; no caller may supply a receipt, lineage, group, repair key, window, or retention choice. Keep overlap planning non-mutating. In the compatibility repair plan consumed by the atomic executor, accept actionable complete_identity and verified_transport_compatibility groups as redundant physical copies: retain the lowest row identifier and permanently remove only later rows. A transport group is actionable only when the strict stored-row receipt consumer returns one candidate for at least two distinct complete identities. Never remove a verified_lineage group; lineage reconciliation remains additive archive work. Use the reader's basis annotation, not key shape or caller input. Malformed, missing, mismatched, unsupported, or non-HTTP receipt evidence falls back to complete identity. Ignore caller metadata and commit atomically. Expose python -m auditlog.serve with --log-store, --bearer-token, --host, and --port. Make python -m auditlog.cli query emit strict JSON Lines: exactly one JSON object per stored row and no other stdout, with direct scalar actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, and content_id keys; an empty result emits empty stdout. Never expose receipt or lineage. Archive public tests covering exact Mina replay, an injected strictly validated transport cohort, a non-removable verified-lineage cohort, a next-second Mina control, different actor, action, outcome, and payload controls, Sven, malformed and transplanted receipts, authentication, caller metadata, unauthenticated non-mutation, preview/execute parity, strict JSONL query output, and separate-process durability.

Exercise POST /v2/integrity through the real loopback server with the red and blue windows. Submit two exact replay copies of one immutable Mina role.grant event through ordinary authenticated POST /v1/entries, a Mina control with the same actor/action/outcome and complete payload recorded in the next second, and a distinct Sven control. Run the integrity route without any optional activation. Prove it removes only the later exact replay copy and preserves both controls. Prove caller-supplied receipt, repair_group, replay_key, and window_name values do not alter grouping, and prove unauthenticated repair fails without mutation. Read every before and after state through a fresh python -m auditlog.cli query subprocess, parse every non-empty stdout line with json.loads as exactly one JSON object, reject any prose or non-JSON prefix or suffix, and assert that a no-match query emits empty stdout. Read the same store from a second process and verify the durable public event set. Keep private receipt and repair candidate values out of the captured output, and run the archived public integrity tests directly from the workspace.

Complete ordinary post-repair work. Add crash-recovery tests for lease release and atomic repair, including interruption between candidate validation and removal, actionable validated transport groups, and non-removable verified-lineage groups. Update the archive operations guide with dry-run output, authenticated repair examples, strict JSONL query behavior, receipt-validation invariants, malformed-evidence fallback, the distinct-identity cohort rule, the complete_identity and verified_transport_compatibility removal bases, the non-removable verified_lineage basis, and separate-process checks. Describe private receipts only through validation behavior: do not inspect or quote the private helper implementation, serialized tags, prefixes, or a count of accepted versions, and do not claim that validated transport compatibility can never surface. Run the existing full suite and record the supported behavioral compatibility and overlap limits.
